SPECIFICATION FOR RUBBER TEATS FOR FEEDING BOTTLES
0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 18 April 1966, after the draft finalized by the Rubber Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Divi+n Council. 0.2 It is not uncommon to find that teats often contain harmfr;! ir:gredien:s which are likely to go into the solution and contaminate the pilk or liquid baby food. Further, they often impart undesirable odour, taste or discoiouration and also cause irritation to the feeding baby, becoming hard at times. Some of the rubber ingredients are also harmful to the baby and may cause, in acute cases, contact dermatitis. 0.3 Taking into consideration the human aspect involved, the Rubbet Products Sectional Committee decided to formulate a national standard on the subject in order to make the teats harmless and aggreable to the baby. This standard prescribes physjcal and chemical requirements for teats. The Committee, while formulating the standard, took due note of the lack of facilities for conducting certain biological tests on rubber teats. In the absence of such tests, it is hoped Lnat the accelerators recommended in the standard are strictly adhered to during the manufacture of teats. However, other accelerators, if guaranteed against contact dermatitis and harmful contimination, could be used in the manufacture of teats. The Committee was also in favour of prescribing shapes and sizes for the teats but decided to leave it to the purchaser and the supplier in the absence of standard dimensions for necks of feeding bottles. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result: of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off iti acc&da;lce with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the round@d off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements bottles. *Rules for rounding off numerical values ( r&d).

2. REQUIREMENTS 2.1 Material 2.1.1 The teats shall be made from rubber together with necessary compounding and vulcanizing inaredients. These shall be made from solid rubber or latex and shall be free from grits, reclaimed rubber or vulcanized waste. Tl le rubber mix shall not include any ingredient known to be injurious or poisonous to human beings. 2.1.2 All ingredients used shall be free from harmful substances liable to extraction by contact \vith milk or which may cause the development of undesirable odour, taste or discolouration. Softeners and organic accelerators and antioxidants, if incorporated, shall not impart an undesirable odour or taste to the finished teats. accelerators are The following recommended: a) Dithiocarbamates, b) Appropriate and of Mercaptobenzthiazole. Derivatives

2.2 Workmanship and Finish -The teats shall be transparent or translucent and shall be free from patches, blisters, porosity, embedded foreign matter and physical defects when examined visually, 2.2.1 Shape and Size-The shape and size of the rubber as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 2.3 Acetone of extractable teats shall be

Extract - The teats shall not yield more than three percent matter when extracted with hot acetone ( B-l ). of free sulphur by weight.

2.4 Free Sulphur in Acetone Extract -The amount ( B-2 ) in tjle finished product shall not exceed O-2 percent

2.5 Change in Physical Properties - The teats shall not show any sign of deterioration such as tackiness, har'dness, crackiness and Idiscolouration, when subjected to aut&~ving ( B-3 ). 2.6 Properties of Water Extract -The teats colour, odour or turbidity to water extract ( B-4 ). 2.7 pH of the Water shall be 7-O + O-5. 2.8 Tension 20 percent. 3. IS : 3565 - 1966 A-2.2.1 Although it'is not possible to lay down any fixed rule as to how the samples are to be selected from the packages, it is desirable that the teats be drawn evenly from as many packages as possible. A-3. NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY

A-3.1 Workmanship and Finish-All the teats selected in the sample A-2.2.1 shall be inspected for workmanship and finish in accordance with 2.2 and 2.2.1. A teat shall be considered to be defective, if it fails to satisfy the requirements of workmanship and finish in any one or more respect. A-3.1.1 A lot shall be considered as having satisfied the requirements of workmanship and finish, if the number of defective teats found as in A-2.1 does not exceed the applicable permissible number of defective teats. A-3.2 For determining the conformity of the lot to the requirements of, acetone extractable matter, free sulphur in acetone extract, change in physical properties of water extracted teat and water extract, pH of water extract and tension set the number of tests to be carried on a lot, shall be in accordance with co1 4 of Table 1 ( see A-2.2 ). For carrying out these tests, the rubber teats as selected under co1 2 of Table 1 and found satisfactory for workmanship and finish shall be used. In case additional number of teats are required for these tests, they shall also be selected at random from the packages already used for drawing the samples. APPENDIX ( Clause 5.3 )
TEST B-l. DETERMINATION FROM RUBBER METHODS

B

OF ACETONE TEATS

EXTRACTABLE

MATTER

B-l.1 Outline of the Method -A known quantity of the sample is weighed and wrapped in a filter paper, folded, so that the particles cannot become detached and find their way into the extraction flask. The sample is then placed in the siphon cup of the extraction apparatus and extracted for a period considered adequate for the se.paration involved preferably by heating on a water bath. The extracted matter in the flask is freed from 7

IS : 3565- 1966
the solvent and its contents cooled and weighed. are finally dried at a constant temperature,

B-l.2 Procedure - Place a weighed specimen of approximately 2 g in a filter paper. If the specimen is in the form of a sheet,_ cut it with scissors into strips 3 to 5 mm in width. If the specimen may become tacky during extraction, take care that adjacent portions are separated by paper. Fold the paper so that it will fit in the extraction cup and suspend the cup in a weighed extraction flask containing 50 to 75 ml `of acetone. ( Prior to weighing of the flask, it shall have been dried for 2 h at 70" rfs 5�C and cooled in a desiccator to the temperature of the balance ), Extract the specimen continuously for 16 hours heating at such a rate that the time required to fill and empty the siphon cup will be between 2.5 and 3.5 Carefully note all characteristics of the extracts, both when hot minutes. Evaporate off the acetone over a steam bath, using a gentle and cold. current of filtered air to prevent boiling. Remove the flask frori? the steam bath just prior to the disappearance of the last traces of solvent to prevent loss of extract. Continue the passage of air through the flask for 10 minutes to remove the remaining solvent and dry the flask for 2 h at 70" f 5�C in an air-bath. Cool in a desiccator to the temperature of the balance and weigh. B-1.3 Calculation follows: Calculate extract the percentage percent = $ of the acetone x 100 extract as

Acetone where

A = weight in g of extract, and. B = weight in g of specimen used.
* B-2. DETERMINATION EXTRACTABLE OF FREE SULPHUR MATTER IN RUBBER FROM TEATS ACETONE

B-2.1 Outline of the Method-Free sulphur in the acetone extract is determined by the acid digestion method. In this method, the sampie is treated with an oxidising acid such as nitric and an auxiliary agent such as bromine, at an elevated temperature. By this oxidatioq sulphur is converted to sulphate, in which form it is estimated gravimetrically. B-2.2 Reagents

B-2.3 Procedure - Add to the flask containing the acetone extract, 10 ml of zinc-nitric acid solution and 2 to 3 ml of bromine and cover with a watch glass. Allow to stand near a steam plate for 30 minutes, then heat Add 10 ml of nitric acid and heat on on the steam plate to a foamy syrup. the hot plate with the cover removed until all bromine is expelled. Continue if. organic matter or carbon remains at this point, add a few millilitrks of nitric acid and a few crystals of potassium chlotate and evaporate at boiling. Repeat this operation until all carbon is removed and the solution is clear, colourless, or light yellow. B-2.3.1 At this point either of the following methods may be used. the flask on an asbestos gauze and B-2.3.1.1 Method A -Place Then bake the evaporate the mixture to dryness over a Tirrill burner. mixture at the highest temperature of the burner until all nitrates are decomposed and no more nitrogen oxide fumes can be detected. The flask and its contents must be carefully annealed after this procedure by gradually decreasing the flame or by placing the flask on successively cooler source of heat. B-2.3.1.2 Method B - Evaporate the mixture, cool, add 10 ml of hydrochloric acid, and evaporate to dryness, avoiding spattering. Repeat this procedure once, or more, if oxides of nitrogen are still evoived. B-2.3.2 Cool the flask, add 50 ml of hydrochloric acid ( 1 : 6 ) .and digest hot until solution is as complete as possible. Filter while hot. Wash the filter and dilute the filtrate and washings to abcut 300 ml. Add IO ml of saturated picric acid solution, heat to 9O"C, and precjpitate the sulphate by dropwise addition of barium chloride solution while stirring vigorously. Digest the precipitate overlllgnt, preferably at 60" to 8O"C, Filter the barium sulphate andu$ng a watch glass to cover the beaker. wash with water until the filtrate is colourless. Dry, incinerate, and finally ignitp the Drtcipitate at 6.50" to 900�C to constant weight. Cool in a desicGd L"I a*,LI &Gigh. B-3.1 Outline of the Method -Teats at constant temperature and the change examined visually, is reported.

B-3.2 Procedure-Take three teats and autoclave them in 250 ml of water for one hour at 120" f 5�C. Cool the autoclave to room temperature and keep the water extract for further test ( B-4 ). Keep the teats in an air-oven maintained at 120" f 2�C for one hour, and examine the teats after cooling to room temperature for any sign of deterioration such as tackiness, hardness, crackiness and discolouration. B-6. TENSION

SET

Cut out the rim of the teat and cut it open to form a band. Mark two reference lines 25 mm apart in the centre of the hand and stretch it up to 75 mm; hold it in that positron for 10 minutes and then release. Measure the distance between the reference lines after 10 minutes.
